az_wheeler_wall.blurb: Wheeler Wall sits in the Mid-Mountain zone of Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson, at roughly 7,500 feet. It holds five single-pitch routes, a blend of bolted slab lines and trad, with grades running from 5.7 up through the 5.11 range. The stone is described as excellent and the slab climbing as steep and demanding. A 60 m rope covers every line, and the way down is an easy, obvious walk-off.

az_warm_up_wall.blurb: Warm-up Wall is a small sport crag in the Virgin River Gorge, in the Arizona Strip of far northern Arizona. It has five bolted routes, a few of them moderate, spanning 5.9 into the 5.11 range. Getting there means going under the freeway and taking the trail that heads left toward the neighboring Blasphemy Wall; this is the first crag along that trail. It is a gentler stop than the harder walls around it in the gorge.

az_3_pillar_wall.blurb: Pillar Wall is a trad crag on the south side of Volunteer Canyon near Flagstaff, set in a bowl of tall columns that stands out from across the canyon. It has five routes, all gear climbs, from the 5.10s into the 5.11 range, so there is little here for beginners. The columnar basalt around it is known for splitter cracks and powerful face moves. The wall faces northwest and stays in shade until very late in the day through midsummer. The faint trails on this side can be hard to find, and rattlesnakes use the cracks in hot weather.
